title: Coordinate cross-team review handoffs and exit criteria for PRD v2
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Purpose: establish a lightweight, time-boxed handoff and acceptance flow for PRD v2 (routing & rollout controls) so engineering/design/legal sign-offs are explicit, traceable, and unblocked by unclear ownership. This ticket coordinates owners, defines per-team exit criteria, lists known trade-offs, and records meeting outcomes to unstick the PRD review. Context: PRD v2 introduces route-level fallback policies, model-variant pinning, and a new rollout UI. Cross-team reviews flagged gaps in RBAC language, latency SLO acceptance, and UI copy for fallback behavior. Goal: Get all teams to a 'review-complete' state with explicit actions or documented exceptions before the release branch cut.
acceptance_criteria: Engineering: Implementation notes and API contract documented in the PRD; ENG review approves the request/response schema and fallback behavior; two engineers named for rollout support; performance budget agreed (p50 < 120ms for control routes, p95 < 350ms for heavy routes).
Design: UX flows and copy updated in the PRD mockups; design review sign-off recorded with versioned figma link and an accessibility checklist (contrast, focus states) greenlit.
Legal/Security: Data residency and telemetry export text approved for Private deployments; legal confirms no new export-control flags; security sign-off on KMS/HSM integration plan.
PM: Acceptance checklist completed in this ticket, all dependencies either resolved or assigned with mitigation plans; release owner assigned and rollout window scheduled.
decisions: Fallback policy default changed from 'best-effort' to 'guaranteed' for premium customers; engineering will implement circuit-breaker with soft-fallback and documented latency trade-offs.
Design will supply compact copy variants for 3 viewport sizes; primary copy will surface exact failure cause when available, with a brief FAQ in the console.
Telemetry: add a new 'fallback_reason' tag to events. Legal approved adding telemetry with hashed identifiers only for Private customers.
open_questions: Does Dedicated mode need a separate rollout UX or is a single flow acceptable with guardrails? (Action: Eng to prototype by 2026-03-09).
What SLO rollback thresholds should trigger automated canary aborts for multi-model routes? (Action: SRE to propose thresholds).
Clarify whether on-prem customers require a different disclosure for telemetry; legal to confirm scope.
meeting_notes: 2026-03-03 sync (Attendees: Aisha R., Liam C., Marisol V., Ravi Patel (ENG), Sana Ibrahim (Legal), Priya Shah (Design)). Key points: Ravi flagged a KV-cache incompatibility in the proposed fallback path; Sana requested explicit telemetry language for Private installs; Priya pointed out truncated copy on narrow consoles. Agreed: engineering will deliver a short design-technical spec by 2026-03-09 and a follow-up review on 2026-03-11. Action owners captured below.
next_steps: ENG: Draft design-technical spec and proto API by 2026-03-09 (owner: Ravi Patel).
DES: Provide compact copy alternatives and update figma file; mark components with accessibility notes by 2026-03-08 (owner: Priya Shah).
LEGAL: Confirm telemetry language for Private and Dedicated by 2026-03-10 (owner: Sana Ibrahim).
PM: Consolidate sign-off checklist and circulate to stakeholders; schedule final gate review 2026-03-12 (owner: Aisha Raman).
